answer: One identity runs one glacier workshop selling crystal pieces, each with a warranty lasting the horizon period. It locks 70 bond and 30 reserve, with each sale key-bound on the ledger. If a crystal fails in the horizon, the buyer claims with the sale receipt; an auditor recomputes the terms, paying a valid claim from the bond and burning a false claim's 10 deposit. The k-th fake workshop needs 100 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 100,000. A warranty-dodging ring fails: a valid claim drains its shared bond, leaving others uncovered. An honest workshop pays 100 once and recovers it after horizon.
